gloss: to hold out; to withstand; to endure

definitions.gloss: to hold out; to withstand; to endure
definitions.explanation: To keep standing under pressure, attack, or hardship without giving way. Somewhat literary on its own; most learners meet it inside the compound verb {持|も}ち{堪|こた}える.

examples.japanese: ⟦{敵|てき}→敵：03546_teki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{攻撃|こうげき}→攻撃：02748_kougeki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧{堪|こた}えた。
examples.english: They held out well against the enemy's attack.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧⟦{橋|はし}→橋：02163_hashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{堪|こた}えた。
examples.english: The old bridge withstood the typhoon winds.

examples.japanese: ⟦{苦|くる}しい→苦しい：02636_kurushii⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧{堪|こた}えた⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦こそ→こそ：12731_koso⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{成功|せいこう}→成功：02638_seikou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: It is precisely because they held out through the hard times that they are successful now.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive. The thing withstood is marked with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ (⟦{攻撃|こうげき}→攻撃：02748_kougeki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{堪|こた}える), and the one holding out is the subject.

USAGE:
On its own the verb sounds formal or written. In ordinary speech it appears mainly in {持|も}ち{堪|こた}える (to hold out, to weather something), which is far more common.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {堪|こら}える: to endure; to hold back — the same kanji read こらえる, used of putting up with pain or suppressing tears and anger
- ⟦{耐|た}える→耐える：12087_taeru⟧: to bear; to withstand — the everyday word for enduring hardship or for a material standing up to stress

NOTE ON こたえる:
The こたえる of ⟦{寒|さむ}さ→寒さ：12336_samusa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧こたえる ('the cold really gets to me') is a different verb, usually written ⟦{応|こた}える→応える：09893_kotaeru⟧ or in kana. Do not confuse it with this one.
